Thanks for the clear markers. From a commercial standpoint Redwood is prepared to offer the following (attached as a one-page amendment and a draft redline):

1) Commit uplift: move from $120k/yr to an annualized $300k/yr commit (12-month amendment).
2) Price hold: Current unit price locked for 75 days from amendment effective date (we set 75 days to align with your 6–10 week window).

4) True-ups: quarterly true-up cadence for months 3/6/9/12 during the first year.
5) Migration milestones: dev verification / stage load / prod ramp spelled out in SOW appendix A. Completion of production ramp is anchor for full commit enforcement.

Hi all —

Quick confirmation from finance/legal: the $12k credit will be issued as an account credit (not a cash escrow). Redwoods's standard practice is to hold the credit on the account and auto-apply it to qualifying overage invoices during the stated 60-day period. We can codify the mechanics in the amendment language as follows:

"Escrow Credit: A one-time account credit of USD 12,000 will be recorded on Customer's Redwood account. During the 60-day conditional period following the Effective Date, the credit will be automatically applied to charges that exceed the agreed committed band. Any portion of the credit not applied during the 60-day period will convert to a non-refundable Service Credit available for use toward Redwood professional services or training and will expire 12 months after the Effective Date."

We will also add the data-handling addendum referencing the SOC2 summary and a 30-day staging artifact deletion requirement. Aditya / Hannah — I'll attach the redlined clause to the draft_amendment_terms.docx and send a final for signature once you confirm the minor edits.
